note: Branch prediction on hardware.  A16's RV32IM figures (docs/a16-benchmarks.json) and A13's RV32I figures (docs/a13-benchmarks.json) are preserved and NOT superseded; this is the same software on the same board with a 256-entry BTB, a folded 2-bit bimodal counter and an 8-entry RAS added.  CoreMark iterations were raised from 2200 to 2500 because A19 made the 2200-iteration run finish in 9.81 s, under CoreMark's own 10 s reporting minimum -- so CoreMark RAW CYCLE COUNTS are not comparable with A16/A17, while CoreMark/MHz and IPC are.

fmax.strategy: explore_postroute (opt/place/phys_opt/route -directive Explore, plus a second post-route phys_opt_design)
fmax.caveat: the search is NOT monotonic: 79.246 MHz failed by -1.186 ns while the tighter 80.998 MHz failed by only -0.676.  Implied path delay for one netlist spans 12.90-13.81 ns, a 0.9 ns spread against the +/-0.4 ns A12 recorded.  77.501 MHz is the highest constraint OBSERVED TO PASS, not a boundary.

predictor.btb_organisation: direct-mapped, tagged, 2-bit counter folded into the entry
predictor.update: at EX resolve only -- a pure function of the retired transfer stream

reproducibility: three JTAG programming passes, four report blocks each, all twelve identical to the cycle (0 ppm); tb/fpga/compare_bench_runs.py agrees across all three passes on 29 invariant and 5 scaled fields
open_item: Dhrystone in SIMULATION at 2,000 runs costs 615.048 cycles/run; at 4,000 and 8,000 runs it costs 609.025 and 609.013, and this board at 200,000 runs costs 609.000.  The 2,000-run point carries exactly 3 extra mispredicts per run (5,998 redirects = 11,996 cycles, matching to the cycle).  It is NOT the image configuration (byte-identical with and without CoreMark and the NTT linked in) and NOT a fixed warm-up cost (that would still show at 4,000).  A18 without the predictor shows no such effect, so it is predictor-specific.  UNEXPLAINED.  Consequence, stated rather than smoothed: the 2,000-run simulation ratio of 1.2633x understates this board's 1.2759x, and a per-run rate taken from a 2,000-run simulation is not a safe proxy for this design.
